title: Descript: how a fired CEO built the editor that edits video like a document
disclosure: AFFILIATE LINK IN DESCRIPTION - AI VOICE

scenes.narration: February 28, 2013. The CEO of Groupon sends a goodbye memo to his staff. One line goes viral around the world: I was fired today.

title: THE FIRED CEO
WHO FIXED EDITING
scenes.subtitle: THE DESCRIPT STORY
scenes.narration: His name is Andrew Mason. And what he built next changed how creators edit audio and video.

scenes.label: GROUPON BOARD
scenes.narration: Groupon had just reported a loss of 81 million dollars in one quarter, and its stock had fallen hard. The board wanted a new leader.

scenes.label: NEW START
scenes.narration: Mason did not stop building. His next startup was Detour, an app of audio walking tours, where a voice guides you through a city, street by street.

scenes.label: AUDIO STUDIO
scenes.narration: But making those tours was painful. The team recorded hours and hours of narration, and editing reportedly took about twice as long as recording.

scenes.label: INTERNAL TOOLS
scenes.narration: So they built themselves a helper. It turned recordings into text, and when you deleted a word in the text, it disappeared from the audio.

scenes.label: DETOUR APP
scenes.narration: Detour itself struggled. Some reports say the app was already doing poorly. But the little editing tool looked like the bigger idea.

scenes.label: CEO DESK
scenes.narration: Mason later wrote that the tool should not stay a servant of Detour. It needed to chart its own course.

scenes.label: LAUNCH
scenes.narration: December 2017. Descript launches as its own product, with 5 million dollars from the investors Andreessen Horowitz.

scenes.label: DEAL ROOM
scenes.narration: April 2018. Mason sells Detour to the audio company Bose, for an undisclosed price, and goes all in on Descript.

scenes.label: VOICE LAB
scenes.narration: September 2019. Descript raises 15 million dollars and buys Lyrebird, a small Canadian voice AI startup. Now you can fix a word just by typing it.

scenes.label: SERVER ROOM
scenes.narration: Podcasters and video makers jump in. Editing starts to feel like fixing a text document, not fighting a timeline.

scenes.label: SERIES C
scenes.narration: November 2022. Descript raises 50 million dollars in a round led by the OpenAI Startup Fund, at a reported valuation of about 550 million.
In 2025, Mason moves to executive chairman. Laura Burkhauser, who joined to lead product, becomes the new CEO.

scenes.label: TODAY
scenes.narration: Today Descript is an AI video and podcast editor. And the idea is still the same: edit the words, and the video follows.
From the fired CEO of 2013 to a tool built for creators. Not bad for a side project inside a walking-tour app.

scenes.label: YOUR TURN
scenes.caption: TRY IT FREE
scenes.narration: So how can you use it? Descript has a free plan. Upload a video, get a transcript, and cut your mistakes by deleting the words.

scenes.label: FREE PLAN
scenes.narration: The free plan has limits, like a small monthly media allowance and a watermark on exports. Paid plans lift those, so check the pricing page.
